topics.title: Line of sight, angle of elevation and angle of depression

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the line of sight as the line from the observer's eye to the point viewed and use it to set up a right triangle.
Recognise the angle of elevation as the angle the line of sight makes with the horizontal when the object is above eye level.
Recognise the angle of depression as the angle the line of sight makes with the horizontal when the object is below eye level.

topics.title: Heights and distances using one right triangle

concepts.learning_objective: Find an unknown height or horizontal distance using tan or cot of a single angle of elevation.
Find the length of an inclined object such as a ladder, rope or kite string using sin or cos.
Account for the height of the observer's eye when finding the height of an object.

topics.title: Problems with two angles of elevation

concepts.learning_objective: Find the height of an object standing on another object using two angles of elevation from the same point.
Relate the length of a shadow to the Sun's altitude and solve problems on change in shadow length.
Find the distance moved by an observer when the angle of elevation of a fixed object changes.
Use alternate angles to show that an angle of depression equals the corresponding angle of elevation.
Find distances such as the width of a river or the gap between two ships observed from a height.
Combine an angle of elevation and an angle of depression observed from one point to find the height of another structure.
